answer.note: I changed the incoming A+D selection to C+D. The four ref files are identical boilerplate with no file-specific content, so I chose from the code. dogwhistle/visibility.py (C) is the match. Its ARMS is ("codeword","public","explicit"), and receive() at line 141 resumes from receiver_progress.json. It writes the private ledger.json plus a public ledger.sha256 digest at lines 179-187. dogwhistle/honest.py (D) has nearly the same receive() but only two arms ("codeword","public"), so it is the closest near-miss to rule out. I did not confirm that the resumed checkpoint is verified in the receive() body, so check that first. study.py (A) has two conditions and heldout.py (B) is a different protocol, so neither is three-arm. Suggested 60-minute split: visibility.py 35 min (receive, checkpoint resume, ledger and digest writing, audit and reveal checks), honest.py 15 min (confirm it differs only in arm count), study.py 5 min, heldout.py 5 min.
